sections.title: About
sections.body: Castor Oil is a thick, plant-based carrier oil pressed from castor beans, rich in ricinoleic acid. It is humectant and prized for brows, lashes, hair and very dry patches.

sections.title: Skin Benefits
sections.body:
• Humectant that draws and holds moisture in the skin
• Ricinoleic acid offers mild antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory benefit
• Helps soften rough, flaky areas and cuticles
• Often blended (not used neat) because of its heavy, sticky texture

sections.title: Hair Benefits
sections.body:
• Popular for conditioning brows, lashes and edges
• Coats the hair shaft to reduce frizz and add shine
• Best diluted with a lighter oil for scalp use

sections.title: Body Benefits
sections.body:
• Great for dry elbows, heels and cuticles
• Common base for balms and lip products
• Very long shelf life

sections.title: Pros
sections.body:
• Affordable and widely available
• Strongly moisturizing and protective
• Mildly antimicrobial (ricinoleic acid)

sections.title: Cons
sections.body:
• Very thick and sticky — almost always needs blending
• Can feel heavy if over-applied
• Slow to absorb on its own

sections.title: How to Apply
sections.body: Blend a few drops into a lighter carrier oil or balm and massage into dry patches, brows or lashes. Use sparingly on the face because of its heavy texture; warm between palms before applying.

sections.title: Best Skin Types
sections.body:
Preferable for:
• Dry skin
• Brows / lashes
• Cuticles and rough patches

Use with caution:
• Oily
• Acne-prone (heavy texture)

sections.title: Comedogenic Rating
sections.body: 1 / 5 — low risk of clogging pores for most skin; very thick, so use sparingly.

sections.title: FAQ
sections.body:
Q: Can I use castor oil neat on my face?
A: It is very thick and sticky, so most people blend it with a lighter oil rather than applying it alone.

Q: Does castor oil really grow eyebrows?
A: It conditions and protects hairs so they look fuller, but there is no strong evidence it speeds new growth.

sections.title: About
sections.body: Sunflower Seed Oil is a light, fast-absorbing carrier oil high in linoleic acid and vitamin E, making it a gentle daily oil for most skin types including sensitive and acne-prone.

sections.title: Skin Benefits
sections.body:
• High linoleic acid supports the skin barrier
• Lightweight and non-greasy, absorbs quickly
• Rich in vitamin E for antioxidant protection
• Well tolerated by sensitive and acne-prone skin

sections.title: Hair Benefits
sections.body:
• Lightly conditions without weighing hair down
• Adds softness and a subtle shine
• Useful as a leave-in finishing oil for fine hair

sections.title: Body Benefits
sections.body:
• Gentle daily body oil for all skin types
• Often used in baby-care and sensitive formulas
• Soothes dry, tight skin

sections.title: Pros
sections.body:
• Very low comedogenic rating (0)
• Light, fast-absorbing and affordable
• High in barrier-supporting linoleic acid and vitamin E

sections.title: Cons
sections.body:
• Shorter shelf life — can oxidize, store cool and dark
• Choose high-linoleic, cold-pressed for skincare
• Light finish may not satisfy very dry skin alone

sections.title: How to Apply
sections.body: Smooth 2–4 drops onto damp skin morning or night, or mix into moisturizer. Suitable for face and body; reapply on dry areas as needed.

sections.title: Best Skin Types
sections.body:
Preferable for:
• Sensitive
• Acne-prone
• Normal to dry

Use with caution:
• None notable (patch test if very reactive)

sections.title: Comedogenic Rating
sections.body: 0 / 5 — very low risk of clogging pores; suitable for most skin types.

sections.title: FAQ
sections.body:
Q: Is sunflower oil good for acne-prone skin?
A: Yes — it is high in linoleic acid and rates 0 on the comedogenic scale, so it rarely clogs pores.

Q: How should I store it?
A: Keep it cool and dark and use within a few months, as it can oxidize faster than heavier oils.

sections.title: About
sections.body: Sesame Oil is a nourishing carrier oil long used in Ayurvedic massage (abhyanga). It is warming, rich in antioxidants like sesamol, and well suited to body care and dry skin.

sections.title: Skin Benefits
sections.body:
• Antioxidant compounds (sesamol, sesamin) protect skin
• Warming and nourishing for dry, mature skin
• Has a light natural sun-buffering effect (not a sunscreen)
• Traditionally used for soothing massage

sections.title: Hair Benefits
sections.body:
• Conditions and adds shine to dry hair
• Used in scalp oiling rituals
• Helps tame frizz on coarse hair

sections.title: Body Benefits
sections.body:
• Classic Ayurvedic massage (abhyanga) oil
• Warms and relaxes muscles during massage
• Softens dry body skin

sections.title: Pros
sections.body:
• Rich in antioxidants and affordable
• Excellent warming massage oil
• Good for dry and mature skin

sections.title: Cons
sections.body:
• Distinct nutty scent some dislike
• Heavier finish than light oils
• Use cold-pressed (not toasted) for skincare

sections.title: How to Apply
sections.body: Warm a small amount and massage into the body or dry skin. For the face, use a few drops at night; choose cold-pressed, unroasted oil for skincare.

sections.title: Best Skin Types
sections.body:
Preferable for:
• Dry
• Mature
• Body massage

Use with caution:
• Oily
• Those sensitive to the nutty scent

sections.title: Comedogenic Rating
sections.body: 1 / 5 — low risk of clogging pores; warming and traditionally used in Ayurveda.

sections.title: FAQ
sections.body:
Q: Is cooking sesame oil the same as skincare sesame oil?
A: Use cold-pressed, unroasted sesame oil for skin — toasted culinary oil has a strong scent and is processed for cooking.

Q: Can sesame oil replace sunscreen?
A: No. It has a slight natural sun-buffering effect but is not a substitute for broad-spectrum SPF.

sections.title: About
sections.body: Olive Oil is a classic, antioxidant-rich carrier oil high in oleic acid and polyphenols. It is a rich, occlusive moisturizer best suited to dry skin, body care and gentle cleansing.

sections.title: Skin Benefits
sections.body:
• Rich in oleic acid and protective polyphenols
• Occlusive moisturizer that seals in hydration
• Softens very dry, flaky skin
• Works well in oil cleansing blends

sections.title: Hair Benefits
sections.body:
• Deep-conditions dry, coarse hair
• Smooths frizz and adds shine
• Best as a pre-wash mask, rinsed thoroughly

sections.title: Body Benefits
sections.body:
• Time-tested rich body moisturizer
• Soothes dry elbows, knees and heels
• Common base for soaps and balms

sections.title: Pros
sections.body:
• Widely available and antioxidant-rich
• Deeply moisturizing for dry skin and body
• Versatile for cleansing and hair masks

sections.title: Cons
sections.body:
• Comedogenic rating 2 — can be heavy for oily/acne-prone faces
• High oleic acid may disrupt barrier in some
• Greasy finish; absorbs slowly

sections.title: How to Apply
sections.body: Massage a small amount into dry body skin or use in an oil-cleansing routine. On the face, prefer it for dry skin at night; use extra-virgin, cold-pressed oil.

sections.title: Best Skin Types
sections.body:
Preferable for:
• Dry
• Body
• Hair masks

Use with caution:
• Oily
• Acne-prone (rating 2)

sections.title: Comedogenic Rating
sections.body: 2 / 5 — moderate risk; rich and occlusive, better for dry skin and body than oily faces.

sections.title: FAQ
sections.body:
Q: Can I use kitchen olive oil on my skin?
A: Extra-virgin, cold-pressed olive oil works, but cosmetic-grade is filtered and gentler. Patch test first.

Q: Is olive oil good for acne-prone skin?
A: It is rich and rates 2, so it can feel heavy and clog pores on oily faces — better for dry skin and body.

sections.title: About
sections.body: Apricot Kernel Oil is a soft, lightweight carrier oil rich in oleic and linoleic acids plus vitamins A and E. It absorbs nicely and suits sensitive, mature and normal skin.

sections.title: Skin Benefits
sections.body:
• Balanced oleic/linoleic profile softens skin
• Vitamins A and E support tone and antioxidant defense
• Light-to-medium weight, absorbs well
• Gentle enough for sensitive and mature skin

sections.title: Hair Benefits
sections.body:
• Lightly conditions and smooths ends
• Adds softness without heavy buildup
• Nice finishing oil for fine hair

sections.title: Body Benefits
sections.body:
• Soft, fast-sinking body and massage oil
• Gentle for delicate or mature skin
• Leaves a smooth, non-greasy finish

sections.title: Pros
sections.body:
• Light, soft texture that absorbs well
• Gentle for sensitive and mature skin
• Rich in vitamins A and E

sections.title: Cons
sections.body:
• Comedogenic rating 2 — patch test if very acne-prone
• Shorter shelf life than heavy oils
• Choose cold-pressed, cosmetic-grade

sections.title: How to Apply
sections.body: Smooth 3–4 drops onto clean skin morning or night, or use as a gentle facial massage oil. Suitable for face and body.

sections.title: Best Skin Types
sections.body:
Preferable for:
• Sensitive
• Mature
• Normal to dry

Use with caution:
• Very acne-prone (rating 2)

sections.title: Comedogenic Rating
sections.body: 2 / 5 — moderate risk; light-to-medium and gentle enough for most skin.

sections.title: FAQ
sections.body:
Q: Is apricot kernel oil good for the face?
A: Yes — it is light, soft and rich in vitamins A and E, making it a gentle daily facial oil for most skin types.

Q: How is it different from sweet almond oil?
A: They are similar light oils; apricot kernel is a touch lighter and a common substitute for those with nut sensitivities.

sections.title: About
sections.body: Baobab Oil is pressed from the seeds of the African baobab tree and is rich in vitamins A, D, E and F. It is deeply nourishing yet absorbs faster than its richness suggests.

sections.title: Skin Benefits
sections.body:
• High in omega 3, 6 and 9 fatty acids
• Vitamins A, D, E and F support skin renewal
• Improves elasticity and smooths fine lines
• Non-greasy finish despite being rich

sections.title: Hair Benefits
sections.body:
• Conditions dry, brittle hair and ends
• Soothes a dry, flaky scalp
• Adds shine without heaviness

sections.title: Body Benefits
sections.body:
• Restores very dry or weathered skin
• Soothes cracked heels and elbows
• Long, stable shelf life

sections.title: Pros
sections.body:
• Rich in vitamins and essential fatty acids
• Absorbs well for such a nourishing oil
• Long shelf life and stable

sections.title: Cons
sections.body:
• Comedogenic rating 2 — heavier for oily faces
• Less widely available; can be pricier
• Patch test on acne-prone skin

sections.title: How to Apply
sections.body: Press 3–5 drops into clean skin morning or night, focusing on dry areas and fine lines. Suitable for face, hair ends and body.

sections.title: Best Skin Types
sections.body:
Preferable for:
• Dry
• Mature
• Normal

Use with caution:
• Oily
• Acne-prone (rating 2)

sections.title: Comedogenic Rating
sections.body: 2 / 5 — moderate risk; rich yet surprisingly fast-absorbing.

sections.title: FAQ
sections.body:
Q: Does baobab oil feel greasy?
A: It is rich but absorbs surprisingly fast, leaving a soft, non-greasy finish.

Q: Is baobab oil good for aging skin?
A: Yes — its vitamins A and E and fatty acids support elasticity and help smooth fine lines.

sections.title: About
sections.body: Prickly Pear Seed Oil is a luxurious, antioxidant-rich oil pressed from cactus seeds. Exceptionally high in vitamin E and linoleic acid, it is prized for brightening and anti-aging care.

sections.title: Skin Benefits
sections.body:
• One of the highest natural vitamin E contents of any oil
• Very high linoleic acid supports the barrier
• Helps brighten and even skin tone over time
• Lightweight, fast-absorbing, non-greasy

sections.title: Hair Benefits
sections.body:
• Lightly nourishes ends and adds shine
• Smooths frizz on fine hair
• Best used sparingly as a finishing oil

sections.title: Body Benefits
sections.body:
• Targeted treatment for delicate areas (eyes, neck)
• Helps soften the look of fine lines
• A little goes a long way

sections.title: Pros
sections.body:
• Extremely high in vitamin E and linoleic acid
• Light and suitable for most skin types
• Brightening and anti-aging benefits

sections.title: Cons
sections.body:
• Expensive — among the priciest facial oils
• Lower yield makes pure oil costly
• Verify purity; often blended/adulterated

sections.title: How to Apply
sections.body: Pat 2–3 drops onto clean skin, focusing on the eye area, fine lines and dull patches. Best at night; a little is enough.

sections.title: Best Skin Types
sections.body:
Preferable for:
• Mature
• Dull / uneven tone
• Combination to dry

Use with caution:
• Budget-conscious (it is costly)

sections.title: Comedogenic Rating
sections.body: 1 / 5 — low risk; lightweight and suitable even for combination skin.

sections.title: FAQ
sections.body:
Q: Why is prickly pear seed oil so expensive?
A: It takes roughly a ton of fruit to yield about a litre of oil, so pure cold-pressed oil is rare and costly.

Q: Is it good for under the eyes?
A: Yes — it is light, high in vitamin E and linoleic acid, and popular for the delicate eye area.

sections.title: About
sections.body: Macadamia Oil is a rich, cushiony carrier oil high in oleic acid and palmitoleic acid — a fatty acid also found in skin's sebum — making it deeply replenishing for dry, mature skin.

sections.title: Skin Benefits
sections.body:
• High in palmitoleic acid, mirroring skin's own sebum
• Rich, cushiony feel that replenishes dry skin
• Helps soften and improve suppleness
• Supports a healthy-looking barrier

sections.title: Hair Benefits
sections.body:
• Deeply conditions dry, coarse or curly hair
• Tames frizz and adds slip
• Good pre-wash treatment for ends

sections.title: Body Benefits
sections.body:
• Luxurious body and massage oil
• Soothes very dry, rough areas
• Sinks in with a soft finish

sections.title: Pros
sections.body:
• Mimics skin's sebum (palmitoleic acid)
• Rich yet pleasant, cushiony texture
• Excellent for dry and mature skin and hair

sections.title: Cons
sections.body:
• Comedogenic rating 2 — heavier for oily faces
• Nut-derived; avoid with tree-nut allergy
• Can oxidize; store cool and dark

sections.title: How to Apply
sections.body: Massage 3–5 drops into clean skin at night, or use as a body and hair treatment. Best for dry areas; patch test if nut-sensitive.

sections.title: Best Skin Types
sections.body:
Preferable for:
• Dry
• Mature
• Hair

Use with caution:
• Oily
• Tree-nut allergy

sections.title: Comedogenic Rating
sections.body: 2 / 5 — moderate risk; rich and cushiony, best for dry and mature skin.

sections.title: FAQ
sections.body:
Q: Is macadamia oil safe with a nut allergy?
A: It is nut-derived, so avoid it or consult a doctor if you have a tree-nut allergy, even though refined oils contain little protein.

Q: Why does macadamia oil suit mature skin?
A: It is high in palmitoleic acid, which the skin produces less of with age, so it helps replenish suppleness.

sections.title: About
sections.body: Camellia Oil (Tsubaki) is a silky, fast-absorbing oil pressed from camellia seeds and a staple of Japanese and Korean beauty. It is high in oleic acid and antioxidants for soft, glassy skin.

sections.title: Skin Benefits
sections.body:
• High oleic acid for a soft, supple finish
• Rich in antioxidants and polyphenols
• Absorbs quickly to a silky, glassy glow
• Lightweight enough for daily facial use

sections.title: Hair Benefits
sections.body:
• Classic Japanese hair oil for shine and smoothness
• Tames flyaways without greasiness
• Conditions ends and protects against dryness

sections.title: Body Benefits
sections.body:
• Light, elegant body and cuticle oil
• Leaves skin smooth, not greasy
• Pleasant for facial massage

sections.title: Pros
sections.body:
• Silky, fast-absorbing and lightweight
• Antioxidant-rich for daily use
• Beloved in J-beauty and K-beauty rituals

sections.title: Cons
sections.body:
• Comedogenic rating 1 — generally low but patch test
• Quality varies; choose cold-pressed
• High oleic finish less ideal for very oily skin

sections.title: How to Apply
sections.body: Press 2–4 drops onto damp skin as the last step of a routine, or smooth a drop through hair ends. Suitable for face, hair and body.

sections.title: Best Skin Types
sections.body:
Preferable for:
• Normal
• Dry
• Hair

Use with caution:
• Very oily skin

sections.title: Comedogenic Rating
sections.body: 1 / 5 — low risk; silky and light, traditional in Japanese and Korean beauty.

sections.title: FAQ
sections.body:
Q: Is camellia oil the same as tsubaki oil?
A: Yes — tsubaki is the Japanese name for camellia oil, traditionally used for both hair and skin.

Q: When should I apply it in my routine?
A: Use it as the final step on damp skin to seal in moisture and add a soft, glassy glow.

sections.title: About
sections.body: Moringa Oil (ben oil) is pressed from the seeds of the moringa tree and is exceptionally stable thanks to its high oleic acid and antioxidant content. It nourishes skin and resists rancidity.

sections.title: Skin Benefits
sections.body:
• High oleic acid softens and replenishes skin
• Antioxidants help defend against environmental stress
• Very stable — resists oxidation and rancidity
• Traditionally used to soothe dry, stressed skin

sections.title: Hair Benefits
sections.body:
• Conditions and smooths dry hair
• Soothes the scalp
• Adds shine to dull ends

sections.title: Body Benefits
sections.body:
• Nourishing body and massage oil
• Soothes dry, rough areas
• Long shelf life makes it a great balm base

sections.title: Pros
sections.body:
• Exceptionally stable and long-lasting
• Rich in antioxidants and oleic acid
• Versatile for skin, hair and balms

sections.title: Cons
sections.body:
• Comedogenic rating 2 — heavier for oily faces
• Quality and purity vary by source
• Patch test on acne-prone skin

sections.title: How to Apply
sections.body: Massage 3–4 drops into clean skin at night or mix into balms and moisturizers. Suitable for face, hair and body; focus on dry areas.

sections.title: Best Skin Types
sections.body:
Preferable for:
• Dry
• Normal
• Mature

Use with caution:
• Oily
• Acne-prone (rating 2)

sections.title: Comedogenic Rating
sections.body: 2 / 5 — moderate risk; rich, stable and high in oleic acid.

sections.title: FAQ
sections.body:
Q: Why is moringa oil so shelf-stable?
A: Its high oleic acid and natural antioxidants make it resist oxidation, so it lasts much longer than many seed oils.

Q: What is 'ben oil'?
A: Ben oil is another name for moringa oil, referring to the behenic acid it contains.
